utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Court Deputy, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no questions for this witness. We agreed yesterday not to ask any questions of this particular witness. Therefore, Dragan Jokic's Defence has no questions for this witness today. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa, now it is your turn.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Re-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us how your friends arrived at Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived with their whole unit in a convoy. And they turned off in Konjevic Polje, took the road from Bratunac, and they went straight to Bratunac. I wasn't there myself, so I can't tell you exactly how they arrived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what vehicle they arrived in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure. There were about 50 or 60 vehicles, so whichever one they happened to be in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people were with you, sir, when you left Bratunac where you say you went to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us their names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother, Miodrag Grujicic, and Gojko Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, what is the colour and type of vehicle that you used to leave Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a military 110, and it only comes in one colour: Green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does it look like? Can you describe a 110.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, it's a lorry. I'm not a driver myself. I'm not a professional driver. I'm not sure what the exact description would be. It was just an ordinary lorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you explain, sir, how is it that a truck from your unit came down to pick you up? How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it always came whenever we had to go on a mission. Someone from Bijeljina would send a vehicle over to pick us up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you, sir, in Bratunac when you were picked up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would usually gather in the centre of town. The lorry would be there to pick us up at a scheduled time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you know what the scheduled time was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would normally tell us by telephone. We would know as a rule. We would find out, and then they would tell us when the lorry would be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It appears that the Prosecutor is doing direct examination as opposed to redirect. Now, in light of the questioning in this particular instance, I don't object. I just do want to raise, however, the issue that it is direct and not redirect. And so in the future, I will be vehemently objecting to Prosecutors coming here and doing direct on their redirect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In principle, I agree with you that the redirect should be within the scope of the cross-examination. There's no problem about that. But the question asked by the Prosecutor is a serious question arising from your questions. So this time I'll let the Prosecutor to move on, and be very careful about that, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. Am I permitted to continue with this line of questioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it depends on how far you'll go.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't believe I'll have too many questions, but perhaps we'll just see what the witness has to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, how did you find out on this occasion by telephone that you had to be picked up in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't only by telephone. My brother would usually know the exact time. They didn't phone me to tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who did they phone, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it was on that day, but those boys who came over from Sarajevo were told exactly what time we would be leaving for Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in charge of your group, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gojko Simic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall precisely where you were picked up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you said in the centre of Bratunac, sir, but is there a more precise location that you can give us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the cinema.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any contact, sir, with any army officers in Bratunac at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no contacts. I did know Momir Nikolic personally, though, but I didn't have any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who specifically informed you, sir, that you were to leave that day and at that scheduled time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Judge Argibay, please. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I have some questions for you. First, can you tell me what was the significance of the bandanna, because I've seen in the video a lot of people using that from different units. And has that a special significance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No special significance. It was just the sort of thing you wore. How should I put it? It was more for teenagers. As you had occasion to see, there were no older, rather mature men wearing bandannas. Those were all young men aged 22, 23. Even here in Holland these days, I see many people walking the streets wearing bandannas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: But not with uniforms, I think.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not wearing uniform, but there was nothing else for us to wear. I wore that uniform throughout the entire war. I hardly wore anything else at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: No, I mean, the combination with uniforms, if you were a soldier at the time, wearing bandannas also.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't forbidden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Okay. That was what I wanted to know. You said you were wearing a NATO uniform at that time. How come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had bought one, or rather, I had traded one for another one that I gave him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: You traded with a NATO soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, with a fellow of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Was it usual to have this sort of NATO uniforms on the market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were many of us wearing NATO uniform. Quite many really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you. I want to know if it was easy to buy these uniforms in the market.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't difficult to come by. And everyone liked wearing it -- everyone wanted one like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to another subject. You said that your group, your unit, was in Bratunac. Then you were picked up for a mission in Brcko. I'm sorry for the pronunciation. Your corps has nothing to do with the Bratunac Brigade. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. But we certainly didn't have any contact, at least not that I was aware of, any contacts with the Bratunac Brigade, with Zvornik, with Birac, with the whole area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: So what was your group doing in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we resided there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: I had understood that you resided in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, only Muslims lived in Srebrenica. I had been born in Srebrenica, but I didn't live in Srebrenica during the war, but rather in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Okay, so you were all living in Bratunac, all the group, and then you were given this mission to go to another town, and then you were picked up by a truck from your unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: And do you know who assigned you to this mission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All missions were handed out to us by Ljubisa Savic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Who was who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the main commander of the Panthers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Was he also in Bratunac by that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were in prison sometime. Do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date. Sometime between the 12th and the 16th, give or take a day or two. I may be mistaken there. I can hardly remember what happened yesterday, let alone ten years ago. Most probably, there should be a record in that particular prison, and it must be reflected in the record of that prison. It may have been the 14th, the 13th, the 15th, but I really can't say with any degree of precision whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Which month? Which year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back then, it was after St. Peter's Day. It was about the 12th of July. It was within the space of those three or four days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Then you were there a very short period. How long were you in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five or six hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: And what for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They caught us holding certain items, or rather goods in Ljubovija that we were not supposed to be in possession of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: You mean for a robbery or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some cheap things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: And were you tried after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-188 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the origin of those goods was not known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any documents to tender into the evidence by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would be tendering Prosecution Exhibits 150B and 150A. 150A is the English translation of the Zvornik hospital protocol book, or at least one particular page of that book. And 150B is the B/C/S original protocol, Zvornik hospital protocol book that I referred to earlier. I would also be tendering, Your Honour, P151, which is an affidavit from investigator Jean Gagnon relating the seizure of the book. As well, P152, which is a log with the draft translation, reflecting that it's a certified true copy of the medical book from the hospital. And those items I would ask to be tendered under seal, Your Honour. Also P154, which is the map; and P155, which is the name of the witness, also to be tendered under seal, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, 150 and 151 -- well, 150, I don't have a problem with. 151, the affidavit, I don't know how it comes in. Technically, I think they have to bring in the gentleman or they must do something or they must make a reference to it. So technically speaking, I don't see how that can come in. And I certainly don't want to establish some kind of a precedent that I'm going to allow the Prosecution to do whatever it wishes, whenever it wishes, without following at least some kind of protocol. Under the circumstances, however, in light of what this is, I have no objections. But I do want to raise for future purposes that the fact that I'm being rather generous today, I will not do so in the future, unless they do it through the proper formalities. There is a way of doing it. As far as all the rest, again, I have no objections. I am rather taken aback that this has to be filed under seal. I would suspect, since there wasn't any explanation as to why it should be under seal, is because the gentleman has asked for protective measures, though I should also note that the Prosecution has repeatedly and without any -- without any previous protections mentioned the gentlemen's name through their other witnesses. So the cat is out of the bag, so to speak. Obviously, they perhaps didn't realise that the gentleman would be asking for these sorts of protections. And frankly speaking, I don't think the protections were necessary. But be that as it may, again, I don't see why it has to be under seal, but if that is the reason, then I leave it to the Court's discretion to decide as to whether it should be under seal or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any problems with those documents tendered by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no objections, no problems with all these exhibits being tendered into evidence. Just one small digression: The maps, too, should be tendered into evidence today. They have been delivered in this form. But if we look at the transcript, it would seem that the distance between Zvornik and Brcko is about 140 kilometres. A question was asked, the question again, and he answered. However, if you look at the map, if you study the scale, you will see that the distance is much shorter. In actual fact, up to 90 kilometres, Bijeljina-Brcko. However, in view of all other evidence, we have no objections to raise. But we shall, of course leave it up to the Chamber, whether the Chamber will accept into evidence these lists from the Zvornik hospital or not, we leave it to the Court's discretion. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Issa, can you give some explanation of why the document P151, the affidavit, should be admitted into the evidence. As you understand, only those documents used through this witness could be admitted into the evidence. I believe this is a rule. But if you could provide us with sufficient reasons, we will consider it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The affidavit is reliable, and it is a form of testimony, if I can put it that way. I don't believe that for description of how the material came into our possession, that we need to call the witness live. And given that it is a reliable piece of document, I would submit that it would be better to have it before the Court in order for the Court to understand how the report or the medical record came into our possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, you know, the affidavit should come into the evidence through other channels. But in this particular situation, I believe that the affidavit is closely related to the medical documents. So we decided that those documents, 150A and B, P151, P152, P154, the map, and P155 are admitted into the evidence under seal. The reason why those documents are under seal, because the name of this witness is mentioned. I believe that in the list of the documents tendered by the parties, the witness's name is also mentioned. So all those lists should also be under the seal. As the maps, I believe that during the proceedings, the witness used that map. As for the distance indicated first by the Prosecutor, then by the witness, that's another matter. So that's why we decided to admit all those documents into the evidence. Mr. Karnavas, are there any documents on your side that you would like to introduce?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I guess there's no documents to be introduced by Mr. Stojanovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Issa, concerning with that map, do you want to introduce it under seal or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So that document, P154, the map, is not under seal. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to help us. When the blinds are pulled down, the usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a good journey back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are we in closed session still?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go into private session just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With the next witness, I was just informed by Mr. McCloskey this morning that when they rechecked the translation of the interview that is approximately 70-plus pages, they found that there were some translation problems. Obviously -- Mr. McCloskey indicates that they're not that significant. I take his word. However, what may not be significant to him may be significant to me. So my preference would be that after the Prosecution does its direct examination, that I be given an opportunity sometime to read this because also, not knowing this, we went ahead and made all the copies of the statement that we had from them so we could be ready in the event we needed to refresh or impeach. So I will need some time. And given that it now appears that we will not have anybody for Thursday, the 23rd, in light of the new updated witness list that we got, that we're not under any particular pressure. So in any event, I may need about an hour or so to look this over, Your Honour. I think it's 70 pages. I don't want to proceed without at least being diligent in my job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could have a longer break. It depends on the time at our disposal, and it will depend how long the direct will last. Maybe the direct will last for this whole day, so you have enough time to do your homework tonight. And as for the arrangement for Thursday, I believe that you remember before the recess, I informed the parties to be prepared for some procedural matters as for the agreed facts and adjudicated facts. If we have time on Thursday, we'll make the best use of the time available to deal with some procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Then it slipped my mind, and thank you for refreshing it so I can be prepared for Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I have been informed by the Court Deputy that the next witness agreed to testify in open session. So we could have the witness now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, did you want to make the introductory remarks that you have been making to the other witnesses? This person fits that same category.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Well, Witness, before we start, I have to remind you certain rules in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. And you have the right to object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate yourself. But however, the Chamber could compel you to answer the question. The testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against you for any offence other than the false testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you first of all tell us your name and spell your last name, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Dusko Jevic, J-E-V-I-C, D-U-S-K-O.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Jevic, you and I met in my office this weekend. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as with other meetings that you've had with the Office of the Prosecutor, the Prosecution with the investigator went over briefly with you your rights to remain silent, your right to have an attorney present. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in knowing those rights, you chose or agreed to speak with me that day over the weekend. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also said that you would testify today, and here you are. So knowing those rights, are you again waiving those rights and speaking freely to us today?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I am talking to you absolutely voluntarily today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what your current job is and where you work.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I'm a police inspector in the Ministry for Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, what does that entail?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: At the moment, I'm involved in preparing plans for training, and also expert analysis of the training programmes for the police and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And back in July of 1995, what was your position?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, I was the deputy -- assistant commander in the special police unit for operative and training -- operations and training. So it's mostly the same kind of work that I'm doing now; that is, the training of the personnel. But at the same time, I was in charge of the training centre which was located at Mount Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that near Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Between Han Pijesak and Jahorina, there is about a hundred to a hundred and twenty kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you briefly describe to us what the special police was back in 1995. What kind of unit it was?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: It was a unit comprising eight or nine units which were deployed out in the field, and it had it its own command structure which was situated in Janja near Bijeljina. The other units were deployed out in the field. One of the units was in Trebinje, one was in Srbinje, one in the area of Sarajevo, one of Sekovici, one in Janja, one in Doboj, one in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many men just roughly were in each individual unit?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: From 100, 120 to about 150. Some units had more, and some had fewer. It depends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the purposes of these units? What kind of work were they trained to do?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Primarily they were trained for police work, but in case of need, they were also sent to the front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just describe their -- the chain of command, who would have been the top person and below.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I told you on Sunday when we talked what I missed from the command structure, which at the time was in the brigade. It's a name. I will now state the commander of the police special brigade was Mr. Goran Savic. The deputy was Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin. The assistant for internal control and security was Milutin Erakovic. The deputy -- the assistant for operative tasks was Mladenko Borovcanin, and I didn't mention him in Banja Luka. And the assistant for personnel affairs was Mr. - just one moment. I'm trying to remember the name - Obrad Saric. The assistant for logistics was Vitomir Kapura. I was the assistant for operations and training. According to the structure scheme, I ranked in fifth place approximately. According to the hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: There were ranks, and I think at the time I had the rank of lieutenant colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Borovcanin's rank?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I think that he had the rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about Goran Saric, the commander of the police?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I think that also at the time he had the rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Goran Saric's superior?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The minister for internal affairs or his deputy were the superior to Goran Saric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in July 1995, do you know who the minister was?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: In 2000, also I was not sure about who the minister was. I know that Mr. Kovac, Mr. Tomo Kovac, was the deputy minister at the time. I will try to recall who the minister was. At the moment I cannot. I know that the person is originally from Bosanski Novi or Novi Grad as we call it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you receive an order or some instructions at about the time of the fall of the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Either on the 10th or the 11th, I was at Jahorina, and I got an order to go with one company in the direction of Bratunac and to wait for further instructions and orders there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I showed you, I believe for the first time, an order dated 10 July which I will have as an exhibit, 157, if we could let the witness see that. And if our technology is working, it should be on your screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Could I please just ask you to focus the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just let me -- it's probably easier for you just to have a copy. If your eyes are like mine, it might help to have this. Now, you had a chance to see this in my office on Saturday. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that is that order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could just -- let's go over the order just a little bit. Do you see as we start in the beginning, we see the 10 July date. And it goes down to the people that it's addressed to you. Do you see your address on this address list?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: You can see the police training camp Jahorina here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was your understanding of this order? What did you actually do pursuant to this order?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: On top of the order, Mr. Borovcanin also came to see me and he conveyed the order that by 1500 hours on the 11th, I have to be in Bratunac; that I need to make the preparations and set out for Bratunac. So I understood that he wanted me as a professional to prepare this one unit and leave for Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So can you describe the unit that you took to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: It's a unit which was made up of deserters who were picked up out in the field, and they were assigned to us in order to be trained. They were equipped with uniforms, long-barrelled weapons, and there was a certain number of bulletproof vests, Kevlar vests that were available to them. They were of Israeli manufacture. So the unit had basic equipment. That is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were any of these deserters, as you call them, picked up in areas outside the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain that.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: They were brought from Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not quite sure of the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any arrangement that you're aware of between the RS and Yugoslavia to transfer such people over to the special police forces from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I was not at that level in order to know. They were assigned to me for training, and that is the only thing that I was able to know. Obviously I found out that they were picked up from the territory of the former Yugoslavia and Republika Srpska, and they were the ones who evaded military and police duty. And they were simply assigned, a number of them was assigned to us, and a number was assigned to the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you tell us again how many men you took to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, don't hold me to it. I cannot be absolutely precise, but it's about a hundred men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many of those hundred were from this deserter category? Just roughly. I know that we can't be exact in these figures.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The majority of them were deserters. There were a couple of people who were the instructors from the police special brigade, and there was also their company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe how these hundred people were divided into units and who was commanding each of the units.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: They were deployed in platoons and were commanded by people chosen by the deserters themselves, and these commanders were assisted by instructors who were actually issuing instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many platoons?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: It's either three or four. I cannot be quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many actual special police officers or instructors were helping you take charge of this group?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Up to about ten men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe the most significant commanders that were under your command.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The company commanders were the most important, and these are the Djuric and Nedjo Nikolic, these two people. Djuric commanded the first company, and Mr. Nedjo Nikolic commanded the second company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's Mr. Djuric's first name?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Djuric Mendeljev.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the hundred men that you brought. Did they come from both the 1st Company and the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. That day, the people who came with me were all only from the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later, did one of the other companies come to the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. On the 12th, the 2nd Company arrived at Bratunac with Mr. Ekonjic, but to Konjevic Polje, even though I wasn't informed about it, so I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What day did you set off with your 100 troops to go towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time did you arrive in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: At about 1500 hours, and I was sent to the Bjelosevac or Bjelovac village to stay there in the village school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to us briefly where that village is in relation to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I will try to explain. In relation to Bratunac, it is in the direction along the River Drina towards -- I think it's the road that leads to Skelani along the River Drina itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think the distance is between 10 and 20 kilometres, but please don't take my word for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you meet up with anybody when you got to the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. With Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: It was after we found accommodation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just roughly what time of day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: In the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive any instructions from him?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, he ordered me to get some officers and a number of men, and to carry out reconnaissance in the Potocari area to see what was going on there and to report back to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Just before dark, we set out. And since we didn't know the area well, he gave us a couple of locals for us to carry out reconnaissance. I wouldn't exactly call that reconnaissance. I would say it was more observation than reconnaissance, the work that we carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he gave you a couple of locals, who were they?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he gave us a couple of locals. It was just one person who was familiar with the area, and I didn't know who the person was. So this person, I think, took us to a place from which we could observe the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if this person was a police officer or a soldier or civilian?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that person was a police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of -- where did you -- what area did you go to to do this monitoring or reconnaissance?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: We went towards Potocari, but then we turned off to the right, to the right of the main road between Bratunac and Potocari, and then on to Srebrenica. There was a hill there that we went to. It was a hillock. I'm not sure how I should explain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make it past the yellow bridge?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't actually go into the Muslim lines?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you able to observe from this observation?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we observed the UNPROFOR base. We observed people gathering around the base. That was the only thing we were able to observe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you report back to anyone after your observation?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I reported back to Mr. Borovcanin. He told me -- night had fallen by that time, and at that time there were talks underway at the hotel in Bratunac between the UNPROFOR commander, General Mladic, and Muslim representatives, talks about the evacuation of the people gathering there. He told me to wait, and that I would receive further orders in due course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you're observing the people in the UN Compound, did you see any military-age men? Were you able to make that out?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: At the UN base, I did not see those civilians there. They were next to the base, outside the base. It was only later that I saw a number of people inside the UN base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that night that you were doing your observation, were you able to make out any military-age Muslim men from your observation point?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The distance was quite large, but you could see people gathering. It was difficult from such a distance, nevertheless, to judge with accuracy and see who exactly the persons were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any report to Mr. Borovcanin about potential military-age men or potential enemy forces in and around the UN base that evening?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I only said that around the UN base, there were civilians gathering, or rather persons wearing civilian clothes, including women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any more information that night from Mr. Borovcanin or any other source?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. Not that night. Mr. Borovcanin ordered me, or rather told me that an agreement had been reached concerning the evacuation of the citizens gathering outside the UN and UNPROFOR base, and that we should go in with a number of forces to secure UNPROFOR and to make sure the evacuation of the people gathered there would begin because an agreement had been reached with the representatives of the Muslim people, he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did Mr. Borovcanin tell you that an agreement had been reached with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: It was about 2300 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you when he told you that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I believe we met at the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who did you think was in command or in charge of the operation personally at that point?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if one looks at the order that I received, the only possible interpretation seems to have been that General Krstic was in command of the operation because Borovcanin was to place himself at Krstic's disposal in terms of commanding our police forces, because Borovcanin was the commander of the police forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you -- what are you specifically referring to in the order which is the exhibit I previously mentioned, 157?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, under item 5, it says: "The commander of the unit, once having reached the destination, must get in touch with the chief of staff." "The unit commander, having reached the destination, must contact the chief of staff." General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there rules related to who is in command when the special police are working with the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The rules that were applied, or rather used at the time in the area had been taken over from the former Yugoslavia where if there was an imminent threat of war or a state of war, the police were resubordinated to the military, to the army, and placed at the disposal of the army to use them as they saw fit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if that was in place for this operation, for your involvement in the Bratunac order?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was in place at the time, this law, or it was supposed to be in place at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any reason to believe it wasn't in place?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't believe I have any reason to believe that. Mr. Borovcanin commanded the entire police forces, so he could have attended certain meetings where tasks were being handed out. And on the basis of that, he issued us with orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt, but if we're going to be discussing rules and asking the gentleman to discuss the rules, I would ask that the Prosecution make reference to the particular rules, and perhaps even show the gentleman which rules he's talking about. Because I think we're getting into the land of speculation at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it depends. Mr. McCloskey, if you believe that is necessary, you could use those rules. But if you don't, just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't, at this point. These rules are very well-known, have been provided to the Defence, discussed by Mr. Butler. Simple rules I don't feel a need to go into them in detail at this point. But, Mr. Karnavas, we can provide him with copies if he needs them for cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you have still have the chance to cross-examine this matter at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It just that it seems they proofed the gentleman, they discussed the rules, it would only seem logical that they would have gone over the rules with the gentleman, so at least we could have an informed opinion as far as what his understanding are to the rules. I do have the rules myself, and Butler has discussed them. But Butler's not the witness. This gentleman is the witness. But thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It seems that everybody knows what kind of rule it is. So if you have some questions, you have the full right to cross-examine this witness at a later stage. You may move on, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So whose understanding is it to you that Mr. Borovcanin could be receiving orders from in this particular operation?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to item 5 of this order, it says: "Ljubisa Borovcanin shall be the commander of MUP, deputy commander of the special police brigade." So according to the chain of command, he was the only one who had permission to attend these meetings, to receive orders, and to forward such orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your knowledge and experience, who do you think from the army would have been able to order Mr. Borovcanin various things?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object to that. It's an open-ended question. It's broad. I think if it tailor-made to the particular circumstances, I might not object. But as it's phrased, I think it's overbroad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as you understand that the Prosecutor should not ask any leading questions, it is a broad question, but the Prosecutor did not ask the witness to speculate. I don't think there's any problem with this question. You may move on, Mr. McCloskey. But I have to remind you, it's time for the break. You may finish this question. Then we'll break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who in the army that was in the area at the time do you think could issue orders to Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll be very straightforward about this. On the ground, Mr. Krstic would have had the authority to issue him with orders, as well as General Mladic who was moving about and actually handing out orders to different people. Those orders were carried out obediently, without any objections being raised. According to the chain of command in the MUP, I think he could have received orders from Mr. Kovac or from the minister, whoever the minister was at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more. Just clarification: What about officers below General Krstic's position? Would they be able to issue orders directly to Borovcanin in your view?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if Mr. Krstic issued an order to his subordinates to pass on to Mr. Borovcanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to object. He's going to ask the witness to speculate now. And he's asking a hypothetical based no foundation. So if he wants to lay a foundation, because the gentleman is from MUP, he's from the Ministry of Interior, he's a police officer, he's not in the army. So if we can have a foundation. I don't even want the gentleman to hear the question at this point. That's why I interrupted and I apologise. But I think we're getting into an area where they're asking the witness to speculate without a prior foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness has answered "I think not." You may ask some questions why he does not think so, or some other questions along this line. But anyway, it is time for a break. Maybe during the break you could think it over and put a good question to this witness. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jevic, as far as your general knowledge regarding military matters, does a general that's in charge of an operation, an army general that's in charge of an operation have the power to delegate his orders to others?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, I think he does have that authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the morning of 12 July. What do you recall was the first thing that you and your unit did that morning? Or what was the first thing that happened to you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to an order that we had received to enter Potocari down the road, we prepared our men, we took the road across the Zuti Most, yellow bridge. And the men from the company took the left-hand side of the road. And the unit from the public security centre in Zvornik took the right-hand side. The essential task was to provide security for UNPROFOR, to provide security for the people assembled there, and for the evacuation of those people who were allegedly civilians to get off the ground. On our way in, we had no problems. It was only when we started going around the UNPROFOR base, to the left from a hill, somebody fired at us from a rifle. This only lasted a very short while. It was very brief, and we took about an hour to reach the position, the crowd of civilians assembled there and the UNPROFOR base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you receive your order from to go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: From Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you receive that order?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: That evening, we met at the police station in Bratunac, and he told me to get my people ready, that we should enter Potocari to provide security for UNPROFOR. And in order to help evacuate the civilians. This, he said, was an agreement that had been reached the same evening between General Mladic, the representatives of the Muslim people, Bosniak people, and the UNPROFOR commander in attendance at the meeting at the hotel in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this what you testified earlier to that you heard at the police station in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else was at the police station in Bratunac besides you and Borovcanin that night of the 11th when this information was passed to you by Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember who was there. I was only there very briefly, for several minutes. I received my order, and I went back to prepare and to get some rest before the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any army officers being there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you started going towards Potocari that morning, which troops were actually with you? I'm speaking of your own troops now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to object to the term "troops," Your Honour. They're police officers. They may be acting like soldiers under certain circumstances, but they're not troops, and I think that it has a subliminal effect of trying to make them into something they're really not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In this context, the troops are the police officers. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we could battle in English whether or not police officers that are acting as soldiers are troops or not, but it's really not intended for any subliminal effect. These guys are armed with rifles, and camouflage gear. I'm not trying to suggest they're army troops; we know who they are. The witness has said who they are. So troops is a very simple way of describing these folks. That's really what they are; they're acting under the command of the army, they're acting as a combat unit. I mean, this isn't a band of traffic police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have to distinguish the people subordinate to the police and the people in the regular army. So long as the distinction is clear, I see no problem with any terminology as troops, as army, soldiers, whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your men, which of your men went with you on the morning of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Three platoons came with me. One platoon stayed back at Bjelovac and Bjelosevac to rest. I think it was at Bjelosevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were your commanders that were in charge of those men that went with you to Potocari that morning?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The company commander was Mr. Djuric, Mendeljev.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned as you approached Potocari that there was another unit, I think you said from the public security centre of Zvornik. Can you describe what that unit is, where they fit into the structure of armed forces.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This was a company belonging to the public security centre in Zvornik. They took the right-hand side of the road and further to the right. They were part of the military formation, the same way we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what this company from the Zvornik security centre was made up of, what kind of individuals?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Those were police officers who belonged to the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this company mentioned in the order that you had -- the 10 July order we had just spoken of, which appears to have been removed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's P157.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's there. Item 2, forces of the public security centre in Zvornik. Or rather, point 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you go with your men into Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us what you saw, what happened.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: When we reached Potocari, we saw a crowd of people there, women, children. We saw some military units passing through, military units, some of which I was familiar with and some of which I did not recognise. We simply stayed there to provide security for the crowd and for the UNPROFOR forces. About 9.30, Mr. Borovcanin, General Mladic met outside the base, the UNPROFOR base, near a house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this, or did you just hear about it, this meeting between Borovcanin and Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I did see them meet. I was near the place where they met. But I was in no position to listen to their conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any information that came from that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I received information that the vehicles to be used for the evacuation of civilians would arrive, and that I was to liaise with the UNPROFOR officer to see how many civilians were inside the base and to enter the base and to see who else was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you this information and instructions?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he tell you anything else?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. After that, we left and went to see a DutchBat officer. We entered the base together and saw an enormous crowd assembled there, including some wounded. Then we went back and waited for the evacuation vehicles to arrive to begin evacuation of those civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we went to the UN base," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to Mr. Borovcanin. I'm referring to myself. I think Djuric Mendeljev was there. And perhaps a couple of other people who were police officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. You stated you saw other units there, some of whom you recognised and some of whom you didn't. Can you tell me first of all how long you were in Potocari on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in the morning, and I stayed until 19 or 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in Potocari on the 12th, what units did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: There were several units there. Some I recognised and some I didn't. They were just passing through. Many units and many groups were coming to see what was happening in Potocari, and a number of units were simply passing through Potocari. One of the units that passed through were the Drina Wolves with all of their equipment on their way to Zvornik, I believe. The military police, I'm not sure, might have been there, and some other military units I didn't recognise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any members of the Bratunac Brigade military police in Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The military police was in Potocari that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: It was probably just the Bratunac military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember telling me over the weekend that it was the Bratunac Brigade military police that were there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have some doubt now whether or not the Bratunac military police were in Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after -- after you went to the UN base, then you said you came back and were waiting for the vehicles, for the transportation. What did you do, if you could describe the rest of your activity?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: After that, I had breakfast near a house. And in the meantime, General Mladic came by. In a way, with one sentence, he practically told us, "Can you police" - let me not say the word - "come with me up to those people." And I took one guy, his name was Dragan Vasiljevic, who happened to be there at the time, and I went with him all the way to the crowd. If necessary, I can say directly what was the original sentence that he stated. Then General Mladic communicated with the civilians. He was distributing food, water, bread to them. I was there next to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it that you heard General Mladic say?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: He told them that they should be patient, that vehicles would come to evacuate them, that this was agreed on, that the Serb army was fair. That's what I heard. That they shouldn't be afraid of anything and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the comment that General Mladic made to you earlier that may be inappropriate?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I will be direct. I hope the Honourable Court and everybody in the courtroom would excuse me. He said: "Do you police cunts dare go with me up there to those people who have gathered?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened after he gave his speech to the Muslims where you were next to him? What happened then?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing. Simply in that area, many came to see this crowd of people. Many people came and left. It was just like a circus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "many people came," who are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Many units came that I didn't know, and many groups of people in various uniforms came to see it. And then they would leave and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then what happened? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: After that, the buses started arriving. I received an order to pull out two platoons and to send them to secure the Kravica/Sandici Road towards Pervan, so for them to secure that road and to remain there with one platoon in order for the evacuation of the civilians to continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued you that order?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were your troops to be commanded by in that area, Sandici/Kravica?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: One of the officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which -- one of whose officers?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Our officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which one?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Someone from Jahorina or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Someone from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Then the buses started arriving, and as they started to arrive, the buses and the trucks, the crowd was let through. Men, women, children, who got into those trucks, we would turn those buses around in front of the UNPROFOR base because this was a very small area. And as the buses or the trucks filled up, they would leave. In conversation in Banja Luka -- during the interview in Banja Luka in 2001, or in 2000, I heard that Mr. Nikolic said that I was the one who coordinated the separation of people in Potocari, together with him. But I responsibly state that that is not so. I just saw those people getting into the buses and the trucks. They were supposed to be evacuated towards Kladanj. But the evacuation went in the direction of Bratunac, Potocari, Konjevic Polje, Vlasenica, Kladanj. So I don't know where these buses or trucks -- where the people were separated in the trucks and the buses. I was not able to know that, and I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any men separated from their families from the crowd in Potocari while you were there on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on the 12th of July while you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: In that period during the evacuation, I was exactly in the area in front of the UNPROFOR base where there was enough room for the buses and the trucks to turn around. Simply for me, as a person, it was important for me to do this as soon as possible because it wasn't nice to watch that crowd in that state. The weather was hot and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of the Muslims abused in any way during that day on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in that area by the UN base that you've described until the transportation stopped that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw any Muslim hit or kicked, pushed on to a bus?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw any men separated from their families and moved into detention locations around the UN base?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports that Muslims were being physically abused on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports on the 12th of July that Muslim men were being separated from their families?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in Potocari on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any men separated from their families on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim -- any Muslims abused in any way as they were getting on the buses or otherwise in Potocari on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports that Muslims were being abused around Potocari on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports that Muslim men were being separated from their families on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. About what time did the transportation stop for the day on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I think it was at around 1900 or 2000 hours. Between 19 and 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July of 1995, did you know who Momir Nikolic was?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I knew Momir Nikolic from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with Momir Nikolic on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Momir Nikolic in Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: When you talked with me, I also said that I did not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know. We have to just kind of go over things. And I know it's repeating. So did you see Mr. Nikolic on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're aware that Momir Nikolic has stated that he communicated with you regarding the transportation of the Muslim civilians from Potocari on the 12th and 13th. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I must say that I, as a man, honourably, on the 12th and 13th, did what I did ordered to do. And the statements by Mr. Momir Nikolic are not correct. And I think that that has nothing to do with me. I, either as a person or as a police officer, would not permit myself to commit such acts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic didn't say that you committed any acts of abuse that I recall. He said that you were just organising the transportation of the Muslim prisoners in regard to what he said about you.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: In order to be direct, in that period -- when it is translated properly in my language, skretnicar is a person who regulates traffic. So on the 12th and 13th, I simply directed the people. I turned around the trucks and the buses. And as people were let through from the crowd and were filling in the trucks and the buses, and then when it was completed, it went on. So that's how the operation was proceeding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this process, did you communicate with any of the other units that were assisting you in this process?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other units assisting you in this process, of organising the buses and transporting the people out of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: There was a company from the Zvornik centre in that region. There was also the military police. There were also other military units. So I really don't know what they were doing. They were perhaps securing the crowd. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Military police, which military police?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you communicate with anyone from the Bratunac Brigade military police that day, on the 12th, or the 13th, to help get this job done?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have any contact with anyone. I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may have been a translation glitch. Just for the record, I think it's clear that the witness said he never had any contact. So what did you do after the buses stopped transporting people?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: We continued to secure the road, Bratunac/Konjevic Polje. This was done in the period, as I stated before, it was also done on the 14th and the 15th. On the 16th, we stopped doing this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we get there - we'll get there fairly soon - let me just kind of work through this step by step. The evening of the 12th when the transportation was finished in Potocari, did you receive instructions what to do next?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I received instructions just to continue to secure the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you those instructions?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that evening on the 12th of July, is that when Mr. Borovcanin gave you those instructions?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so where did you go after receiving those instructions from Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I went to Bjelovac for a rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about your men? Where did they go?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Some of them were in Bjelovac resting, and some were securing the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know roughly how many went to secure the road?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I think there were two platoons securing the road, and that the rest were taking a rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to try to clarify, when did these two platoons get broken off from your units to secure the road? What time of day on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Sometime after 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So by the end of the transportation which you say I think was at 1700, had those two platoons been out on the road for several hours as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The transport did not last until 1700 hours, but until either 19 or 2000 hours. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, I'm sorry. At 1900 hours, how long had your two platoons that had been diverted, how long had they been out there on the road just roughly?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: That means that after they received the order to secure the road, left to do so. So they could have arrived there in about one hour, to that road that they were supposed to secure, and to deploy along it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how many of your special policemen from Jahorina were in Potocari on the 12th of July, sort of after your other crew went to the road?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Only one platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how many men was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: About 30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So by the end of the transportation, you say 1900, roughly how many of those 30 went where?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Of the three platoons that came to Potocari, two went to secure the road, and one platoon remained in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But now the evening of 12 July, the platoon that's left with you, where did it go after the transportation was over?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: We were pulled back to rest in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So none of your platoon that night that were with you in Potocari the whole day were diverted to the road? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: That night, no platoon was sent to the road except those two that were already there, and then the next day, another company came from the direction of Konjevic Polje to Pervani to secure that road, the people who were -- that platoon which was pulled out on the 12th from Potocari, it went to rest in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, this new company that came on the 13th, where did that company come from?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The company did not arrive on the 13th. It came on the 12th. It came from Jahorina and was stationed at the school in Konjevic Polje with the task of securing the same road. But on the 12th, I didn't know that it had arrived, and I didn't know that it had been deployed. I received this information later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that's the same company you referred to earlier in your testimony that you didn't know about at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did anything happen on the night of the 12th where you were billeted at the school in that town near Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of your men assigned any duties in Bratunac town the night of the 12th, early morning hours of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any Muslim prisoners detained in Bratunac town the night of the 12th, morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do in the morning of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any particular duties on the 13th, so I don't know at what point in time I went to visit the road and see the men, and then I came back to the Bjelovac base to rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to Potocari on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
