utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the first thing you --

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. I apologise. The evacuation also proceeded on the 13th. I apologise. So on the 13th, I was there for the entire time in Potocari during the evacuation. I apologise. I mixed up the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No problem. So in the morning of the 13th, what was the first thing that you did?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th in the morning, we got ready and went to Potocari again to proceed with the evacuation of the civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe that -- your day there.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Just like the previous day, vehicles arrived. People got in, and civilians left. I don't have anything particular to say about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you communicate with any army officers or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any particular instructions from Borovcanin or anyone else on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. My only task was to complete the evacuation of civilians that day, and simply what we were doing, turning the buses around and the trucks. That was it. And to keep things running.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, just so we're clear, on the 13th did you see any abuse of any Muslims in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any separations of any Muslim men on the 13th in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about what time did the transportation finish up on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the evening. I know that we withdrew at about 2300 hours to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry. Let me take you back briefly. When you withdrew from Potocari on the evening of the 12th, did you leave any of your men behind to secure the area around the UN Compound and the civilians?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. Our men were pulled out then from Potocari, and they went to rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who, if anyone, was left to secure the UN area and the civilian area that night, the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't, believe me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next morning, on the 13th, you didn't check in with anyone or see anyone that had been on duty that night?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you're smiling?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, it has been eight years since. You try to think back. You try to recollect every single detail, but you simply can't. What I can say is that I did something that was normal and useful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Potocari on the 12th and 13th, your activities were normal and useful. Okay. On the evening of the 13th, was the job finished?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims left behind in Potocari that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim wounded remained in the UNPROFOR base. And later, I'm not sure in what way exactly and pursuant to which agreements, those people were evacuated. I'm not sure where to, nor who by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you and your troops do that evening when the job was finished, on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: We pulled out and went back to the school where we slept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you drive through Bratunac on your way to the school where you were billeted?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of your men assigned to duties, guard duties, in Bratunac town that night, the night of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they assigned to any duties in Bratunac town the night of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they all go back with you to the school?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that night that there were thousands of Muslim prisoners being detained in the city of Bratunac on the night of the 13th, early morning hours of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reports of what was going on along the road Sandici/Kravica/Bratunac on the day of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first get information about what was going along -- what was happening along that road on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you the exact date, the 13th. I did hear about an incident involving our unit from Sekovici. This unit captured a number of Muslims, or rather, they surrendered to the unit and were billeted somewhere at a factory or a school building. I heard that the deputy commander had been attacked and that they had tried to kill him, the man who was in command of that unit. And then after, that there was a reaction where those people were killed. I heard people talk about this. Of course, the deputy commander reached for his rifle as he was grappling with those people who had attacked him, and he got burned, after which he was killed I think several months later in 1995. He was killed on the Odred [phoen] front. I think his name was Cuturic, his first name was Rade, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first hear this story involving Mr. Cuturic and his burns?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I can't say for sure. Last Sunday, I think we talked about it. I told you I heard the story after the incident had occurred and about what happened later. And allegedly, he burned his hand as he reached for the rifle, as he was grappling with his attackers. Any further comment on my part would, I believe, be superfluous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On the 13th during that second day of transportation, did you have a chance to actually go along the road Sandici/Kravica area?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Now, whether it was on the 13th or the 14th, at any rate, I did visit men there. But I can't say for sure because I may get the date wrong. I'm more inclined to believe that it was on the 14th because between the 13th and the 14th, the men who were providing security along the road had been attacked. Someone threw a bomb at them, a hand grenade. Three men were wounded, two were seriously wounded, and one was lightly wounded and that's why I went there, to see what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever leaving your duties in Potocari of transporting all the people to go along the road, or did you go along the road after all the transportation was over? Just to help you put this in context for your memory. I believe you told us before that it was on the 13th that you did this.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. On second thought, I think I did this on the 14th for the same reason that I've just given you. If I were to say something specific to you now, I am afraid it might be wrong, because there were so many events happening at the same time. I think it was on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the story you heard about Mr. Cuturic and the killing of the Muslims, can you give us any kind of an estimate of how many days after the event you heard that story?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: It may have been the same evening. This sort of information spreads rather quickly. People talk. It's a comparatively small area. I think I heard about this that same evening because people were talking about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you hear about it from?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: From the public commissioner. All the lads from the unit were talking about this. I don't think any one of them told me anything particularly important or specific about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard it from the public commissioner. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. We have a saying, public secret, that's when people talk about what's happening. I simply heard people talk about what had happened, and this is the way in which I'm bringing it up with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask for a report from your commanders that were in the area of Sandici and Kravica?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think they were near that building. I think they were far from that building. I didn't request a report because they had nothing to do with that. One of the reasons is that the 2nd Sekovac Detachment was not under my command, therefore I could not make such a request. They operated in the area independently. I assume they were receiving their orders down the chain of command, meaning from Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any request of Mr. Borovcanin what happened, about this incident?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. We never discussed this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the 14th, the day after the Muslim transportation is finished in Potocari, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: To Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you -- what did you do that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I got some rest. As simple as that. As I said, I went to see those people, and I believe, or rather, I'm sure that I went to the hospital in Zvornik to see how the wounded men there were doing. And after that, I returned to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go see your men that were stationed along the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac Road?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- where did you see them stationed along that road?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Just next to the road itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around what villages?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the whole length of the road, between Kravica and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you check in with any particular commanders?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I believe I talked to Mr. Nikolic who was in charge of the 2nd Company, and I asked him whether there were any problems and that was all we talked about. Yes, of course I did talk to people who were near the scene of the incident when it had occurred, those three men who had been wounded, two severely and one lightly, wounded by hand grenade. And the person who had thrown the hand grenade at them managed to escape down the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to talk to the -- Mr. Cuturic or anyone else who had been wounded at the warehouse incident?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you checked in with your people along that road on this day, the 14th of July, did you receive a report on what they had been doing on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: They were simply there providing security along the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any information about special police forces being involved in the capture of Muslim prisoners along that road on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You got no information about Muslim prisoners captured along the Konjevic Polje/Bratunac/Milici Road on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the 14th of July? When you were going along that road, did you go by the warehouse in Kravica, the large agricultural warehouse there right outside of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I drove down the road and passed the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you heard about the stories by then?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I believe I had heard the stories, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you look over at the warehouse when you went by it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I simply had no desire to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, were any Muslims prisoners captured or did they surrender along that road on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you go the night of the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I believe I was at Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With who?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: With my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of your -- of your men were with you at that point on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I believe there was one reserve platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th, nothing. I got some rest. I spent some time in Bratunac, some time in Bjelovac. I met Mr. Borovcanin. I think I went with him to see Mr. Deronjic. We had coffee together, because Mr. Deronjic and Mr. Borovcanin were talking about something, I believe, but only very briefly. And then after that, I went back to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Deronjic and Mr. Borovcanin speaking about?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember. All this time we were just having coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, some premises or other. It was on one of the upper floors in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th, we received another order to pull the people out from the road, to allow them to get some rest and to organise a patrol that would patrol the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje Road with two vehicles, and a BRD that was at the disposal of the public security station in Bratunac. I think we started patrolling without the BRD at first because it needed fixing. It was not in working order. There were some technical problems with that particular piece of equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you receive the orders to do this from?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: From Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later on, did he give you any other instructions regarding anybody else?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th in the evening, I received an order to report to the Bratunac Brigade about 2300 hours. There was to be a meeting held at the brigade concerning the clearing of the terrain, or rather the searching of the terrain in the general area of Sandic, the area between Srebrenica and Konjevic Polje, the entire area through which Muslim forces, Muslim combat forces, were moving that were pulling out of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt, but I'm told that the gentleman had indicated that concerning the searching of the terrain is what he had indicated, and it appears on the monitor that it says clearing of the terrain. I know it's a minor technicality, but perhaps -- and it's on 21:11:54. So perhaps that could be looked into later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I thought he said both and corrected himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe there's a difference between the clearing of the terrain and the searching of the terrain. Maybe you could ask some questions to this witness, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we clear up that issue, was there so many mention of Momir Nikolic that evening?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I received an order to report about 2300 hours to Mr. Nikolic, to organise a meeting. I went there at 2300 hours, and I was told that the next morning between 7.00 and 8.00 there would be a meeting at the Bratunac Brigade command concerning an agreement to search the terrain or ground. I apologise. There's a huge difference between clearing the terrain and searching the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll clear that up when we get there. We understand. Thank you. Now, who told you to meet with Mr. Nikolic at the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went to the Bratunac Brigade that evening, who did you meet with?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I met with Mr. Nikolic. He told me that there would be a meeting concerning the searching or the combing of the terrain the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything else discussed?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so what did you do?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing. I went back to my base. I told the men to prepare for the next day's meeting, and that we would go out and search the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were at the Bratunac Brigade that night, did you see -- besides Momir Nikolic, did you see any other officers of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I saw some people. But, well, you know, I didn't know those people, and whatever I tell you now -- it was a command. They were supposed to function properly, and it did. I did see people there, but I didn't know the names of those people. I apologise. I must say, as soon as I enter the building, walking passed the duty officer's room, that was the procedure there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if you saw or were introduced to the commander of the brigade that night?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Vidoje Blagojevic at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the next morning, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the next morning, I went to the meeting which started at 7.00 or 8.00, but I can't say. I went to the Bratunac Brigade where the method which would be used in searching the terrain was agreed. We agreed where to start, how to deploy the forces, and there was an agreement as to which forces exactly would take part in searching the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was at this morning meeting at the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were quite many officers. I didn't know those officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Momir Nikolic there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in command of that operation as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as for the police forces that took part in searching the terrain, we took part, and another unit with trained search dogs took part. There was another unit that was with us, a special company from Bijeljina. As for the military, I think there was a unit from the Bratunac Brigade, one from the Milici Brigade, and that was that. Now, as to who coordinated the entire operation, I believe we communicated with the staff of the Bratunac Brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the staff that you communicated with?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who was in overall command of this operation?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Captain Gavric was in overall command of this operation. And it could have been me on behalf of the police forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was Captain Gavric?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Captain Gavric was a man who was in charge of the people from the Bratunac Brigade. Or rather, who commanded the military on the ground, the military carrying out the search.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your forces under the command of the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so who in the army was commanding your forces as you recall?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we received our orders through Captain Gavric. He was liaising and coordinating for that particular aspect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you search the terrain that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The start line was, I think, Kravica, Pobudje, and so on and so forth. It was that area. And then we set out in the direction of Konjevic Polje. And we combed the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any Muslim prisoners that day?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: That evening, just before dusk, about 200 Muslims surrendered, and four children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were done with the four children?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: They were taken over by Captain Gavric, and I don't know where they went from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And roughly how old were these four children?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: From perhaps just over 10 to about 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's lunch break. I'm almost done, Mr. President. I have a few exhibits, few photographs, and so hopefully shortly after the next session -- or during the next session, I'll be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you mean you still need about 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I hope 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. As you know, Mr. Karnavas asked for a longer break. So it's now 12.00. So we could resume at 1.00, and I give you 15 minutes to finish your direct. And the rest of the time will be in the hands of Mr. Karnavas. We'll resume at 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.01 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jevic, we were talking about the 17th of July, and you mentioned that the four children were handled by Mr. Gavric. What happened to the I think you said approximately 200 prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The buses arrived. They were boarded on the buses, and they went in the direction of Zvornik. I don't know where they were taken. But they went in that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the men get on the buses?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: There, where they surrendered, where they were captured on the road. On the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near what village?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember now. The search operation began sometime between 14 and 1600 hours. We started out from the position of Sandici, Ravni Buljim, Pobudje and further. I need to mention that the terrain was very difficult to sweep. At one point fire was opened at us, so I don't know whether this was in the region of Sandici. I cannot really say precisely, but I know that this did happen. This was just before dusk, just before it got dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it along the road between Konjevic Polje and Bratunac that they got on the buses?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Bratunac/Konjevic Polje or Konjevic Polje/Bratunac; it's the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Can you narrow down the rough area at all along the road? If you don't know the precise village, could you break it down a little, give us a little better idea?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to show you an exhibit. It's P159. And I'll just give you the B/C/S. It's a document that I showed you in my office that has got the name handwritten at the end of it, Ljubisa Borovcanin. And did you have a chance to read this document in my office?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen this before, before I showed it to you in my office?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it look like to you? What do you think this is?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This is some kind of report about the events. So I can see that it was signed by Mr. Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I have a dilemma about the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What's that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The dilemma regarding the signature is we worked together, so I know more or less how he signs documents. It's quite close to his signature, it resembles his signature, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the various events that are set out in this document, they have to do with the special police forces and their various engagements after receiving the order of 10 July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything that you've read in this document that just appears to be absolutely incorrect or wrong?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This is a general document, so I cannot really comment on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you've -- you don't know -- do you have any reason to believe Mr. Borovcanin has written this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I have no reason to believe or disbelieve. This signature of his does not look authentic to me, so I cannot -- I would be lying to you or to this Court if I were to say anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it may have been a translation problem, but we had thought you'd said before that it looked, it looked very similar to his signature. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it seems to me that it resembles his signature, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. If we could then just briefly go back to the 10 July order, which is 157. I notice in paragraph 2 of this order, it says: "There's a mixed company of joined MUP forces of the RSK, Serbia, and Republika Srpska." Are you aware of any MUP men, MUP personnel from Serbia that took part with these other forces after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about members of the MUP from Serbia, but based on this order you can see that it's a joint or a mixed company of the RSK, and it was sent to that area. I didn't have the opportunity to see it in that area, but it is beyond dispute that it was in the area of Trnovo and Sarajevska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was a Serb MUP unit in the area of Sarajevo. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, not the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Serbia, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska; that's the one that I meant. I know of that unit, that that unit was in the area of Trnovo, and that's what it states here, the RSK MUP. I don't know about the men from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there is a reference to Serbia MUP here, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You have been shown a series of photographs and video stills. Well, you saw some photographs in my office over the weekend, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we're going to show you some of those same photographs up on your screen. And the first one should be P22, chapter 16, page 5. First of all, do you recognise the large face on the left-hand side of this screen?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Mendeljev Djuric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've described him as being one of the commanders under your command?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: He was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where this -- do you recognise this scene in the backdrop?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the area of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you working around this same area on the 12th and 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I was working a bit lower down. I was working in that area, but I was working a little bit further below. I don't know what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to the next one, 22, chapter 16, page 5 -- sorry, page 6. The person with the -- looks like a blue vest, do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This is a member of the company who spoke English and who communicated or mediated between the gentlemen from UNPROFOR, and he was translating for Mr. Djuric, I assume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In particular, what company?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This company which was in Potocari, the Jahorina company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next one, which should be chapter 10, page 6 -- sorry, it turned black and white. But can you make out anyone in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This is General Mladic, myself, Dragan Vasiljevic, and the escort of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you start on the left side of the picture and describe who the first face is with the sunglasses.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: From my left or from my right? Well, the first person from the left with glasses, that's me. And the person in front that you can only see the arm, I don't know who that is. The second person is Dragan Vasiljevic. Then General Mladic. And then three of the members of his escort. The person to the extreme right with glasses is the first person in the escort of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's go to the next one, which is chapter 12, page 6. How about this person on the far right of the screen closest to us?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: This is a member of the company from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a regular special police guy or is he one of the deserter fellows?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, he's a deserter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to chapter 18, page 6. How about this fellow? Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: A member of the Jahorina company, deserter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next one, chapter 18, page 7. How about this guy?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The same, member of the Jahorina company, deserter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The previous guy, did you know his name either?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Chapter 18, page 10, how about this guy?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Also a member of the deserters' company. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Chapter 18, page 11. What about him?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have any idea where any of these individuals were actually standing in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I think that they were standing along the road that they were securing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions. I hope I made my 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jevic. Should I call you Stalin? Which one would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: You can address me as Mr. Jevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you also go by the name "Stalin." Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's a nickname that you earned because I understand you were a tough disciplinarian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. I mean, you can take it like that as well. But I got this nickname before the war while I was working at the republican secretariat for internal affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina in a special unit of the republican secretariat. At the time, my colleagues named me Stalin because I made them work hard in a disciplined manner on the tasks that we were prepared for or trained to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So I take it you're a man that believes in discipline.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I suspect, perhaps because of your reputation, that is why you were also given the task of being in charge of this training centre. And of course, your qualifications as well.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: That was my job, to be in charge of training. That's what my official post was. I was deployed to that -- assigned to that post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Are you an educated man, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends on what you consider.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you gone to school beyond high school?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I completed first level of higher education.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how many years was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that a police academy?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No. It was the higher administrative school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever attend a police academy or an academy of sorts for police officers?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: From 1973 until 1976, I completed the police academy in Sarajevo. Actually, it was called the militia school at the time. It lasted for three years, and that was my profession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it by the time Srebrenica comes around in 1995, you have approximately 19, close to 20 years of experience as a police officer. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it a lot of it was on-the-job training?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: The knowledge that I acquired in those conditions is relative. According to circumstances in some other countries, and according to the education of people who perform certain tasks, perhaps it is not quite enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you must have had some endearing qualities if you were promoted to the position that you held by the time Srebrenica came in 1995. Wouldn't you say?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you must have been qualified, or your supervisors and superiors must have seen something in you in order for you to get promoted.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: In order to be promoted, it goes without saying that I had to meet certain conditions. In wartime, which qualifications would have been required, that's a different question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you were in charge of training. So is it not fair to say that by that point in time when they appointed you to train others, that you, sir, were qualified for that position?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I was qualified for that position, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And you held a fairly high position by the time you went to Srebrenica back in July 1995, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was a high position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you indicated that below Borovcanin on the ground, there was you. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And between you and Borovcanin, there was no one else. Am I correct on that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And below you, there were about a hundred men that you were responsible for. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we all answered to Mr. Borovcanin. That was the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And below you was also a lieutenant colonel, as I understand it, Mane? That was his nickname, Mr. Djuric? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and Mr. Nedjo Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so these were officers, high-ranking officers, that were below you that you were in charge of. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: They were subordinated to me, and I in turn was subordinated to Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Saric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question now. You were in charge of them; you were responsible for them; you were giving them orders and they were answering to you. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was giving them orders, and they were responsible to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it as a police officer over the years, one of the skills that you develop is the skill of observation. Would you not agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I was never trained for that especially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And today you are an inspector. Is that -- is that one of your titles?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm an inspector. I draft training programmes and general training, specific training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, before you can train, you have to know how to do it, right, how to inspect?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, of course you need to have command of the methods with which you will then use to train people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, of course. And one of the methods is to observe, to be able to go out and look and see and assess what's happening within your eyesight. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it - we just saw you in the photograph - back on July 12th, 1995, you had sunglasses on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was to prevent the sun rays from interfering with your powers, your God-given powers of observation. Right?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the sunglasses, you know, you wear them to protect your eyes from the sun, don't you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, okay. They were pretty stylish as well, but thud them more or less -- aside from the fact that you wanted to be stylish, you had them there to protect your eyes so you could see better under those conditions with the sun shining in your eyes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, is that a relevant question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to get to it, Your Honour. I believe it is, but I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, help me out, here: I find it rather incredible that someone who is a trained inspector, a teacher, with good eyesight, who is also protecting them with sunglasses is unable to see anything that's happening in Potocari on those two days, the 12th and the 13th. Could you help me out here. How is it that you were unable to see anything?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I told you what I'd seen. As for anything else, I didn't see anything else. In that sense, I think I did make myself very clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I guess -- but I'm asking you to help me out here. How is it that everybody else is able to see things, and you, an inspector on the ground in charge of a hundred men, is unable to see anything? How?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Well, how I was unable to see anything, I did see people, women, children, I saw the buses, I saw the evacuation that was underway and so on and so forth. That means I told you what I'd seen. I can't tell you anything that I didn't actually see. It would be quite superfluous to talk about things that I didn't actually see. That's how it was, Mr. Karnavas. Not for a single moment as a human being, and now I'm answering a different question, with the Court's permission, of course, when you expect someone to train deserters, that is an act of humiliation for that person who is expected to carry out that task. That's my view. That was my angle of looking at those things. When those deserters were handed over to me, that was a humiliation for me as a human being because I was educated to respect everyone, to esteem everyone. What I'm telling you now is a very general fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we just saw some photographs of the deserters. I don't know what you saw, but they seemed well fed, very well dressed, and extremely well armed. What do you think?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I think they were poorly fed. I think they were poorly armed. And I think their general -- the way they looked was quite miserable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, Mr. Jevic, it's not permissible for me in this context to use blunt language, but let me put it this way: I believe your testimony with respect to what you were unable to see on the 12th and 13th is dishonest. What do you have to say to that? I think you are being dishonest in this courtroom, having taken an oath to tell us everything that is true.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, Your Honours, I am being utterly honest. I have not a single reason as a human being to say or talk about anything that I did not actually see with my own eyes. Please, try to understand this. I may say some other things eventually, but please, don't force my hand to say something that I didn't see and something that I was not aware of. And that's how it is, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If I could show you -- let's move to another topic, then. And I want to -- we're going to move backwards. I'm going to pick up where the Prosecutor left off. I would like you to look at what has been marked for identification purposes as P159. That was a document that was shown to you with the signature that is purportedly to be Mr. Borovcanin's signature. Now, I understand that you have some reservations with respect to this document, not having seen it before, and not being able to verify completely whether this is Mr. Borovcanin's signature. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the document as was pointed out by the Prosecutor, and I assume that this was shown to you before coming here today. Was it?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it describes certain events over a period of time starting with, I believe, -- well, on the second page, it says July 12th, and then 13th, 14th, then 15th. And then we get to 16th and 17th and 18th and 19th, all the way through the 20th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Will you please repeat this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. From the document itself, it seems to have a narration, at least from the first page, and I apologise, it starts from the 10th, 11th, 12th of July, and it's a summary of events all the way to 20 July 1995. If you look on page 4, you'll see that's the end date. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I left from the ground on the 19th of July. Now, as to what happened in the area after the 19th, I couldn't say. But I did hear about certain things happening. As for this document, I've already given you my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm not asking for your opinion yet. Right now, we're just trying to establish that this document here which has your superior officer's signature to it, or purported signature, seems to be a summary of events dating from the 10th of July all the way to the 20th July.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I came to the area on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we just established -- we just established that you are an educated man. Surely you can answer a simple question. Now, my question is this document itself - I am not asking yet about the contents - this document, does it not seem to be describing in rather general terms events that took place from the 10th of July through the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: I can't answer this question if I'm not sure at all who signed this document, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to verify who signed it. I'm asking you, does it not give a general description of events that MUP were involved in from the 10th of July to the 20th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Now, in looking at this document, which you have seen before coming into this courtroom and which you had the pleasure of going over it with the Prosecutor, do you not find your name in this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I'm not sure about who signed this document. But I did find my name in it, and I was in the area. I did say that. And I am here today. This is something that I have not tried to contest for a single moment, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that you saw your name in there. And I take it where your name is, it describes events or activities that you might have been involved in, does it not? I'm not saying whether it's true or not, but the document does contain your name in relation to activities that you might have been involved in.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I have given you my opinion on this particular document, and I also told you about all the things that I had taken part in. I have no reason to avoid anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jevic, I'm not asking for your opinion. I am asking whether in reading this and seeing your name, does this document not also have your name in relation to activities that you and your men were engaged in at the time during this respective period?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: That is in the document. But as for the connotations and how it was written, when asked by the Prosecutor, I told the Court what happened and how.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Thank you for that answer. Now, if we could move to page 4 of your document, the B/C/S version, the Srpski version, are you able to read this document, sir? Are you able to read it? Is it legible enough for you to read?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, when we get to the date July 17, 1995, okay, there's nothing about you in it having to report to the Bratunac Brigade or to Momir Nikolic -- let me back up. On the 16th, there's nothing about you having to meet with Momir Nikolic at the Bratunac Brigade, is there? I'm not saying whether it's accurate or not; I'm just asking whether it's in the document. It's a simple yes or no answer -- question, I should say.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Here you have listed a number of activities, as far as I can tell from looking at the document. Now as for me reporting to Mr. Nikolic and the meeting at the Bratunac Brigade, it's not here, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And we go to the 17th, there's nothing about you attending any meeting with any -- with the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, so you could be subordinated or resubordinated or however you want to put it to the Bratunac Brigade, is there?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: No, there isn't, sir. I'll repeat this. I have given you my opinion on this document. I told you what my thoughts about it were. But if you allow, I'll look at this document and tell you again. "The 18th, two MUP companies from Jahorina continued to comb along the Pobudje-Nova Kasaba axis."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I was getting to that. The 18th follows the 17th and precedes the 19th. But that's what I was getting at. On the 18th, we do have some mention that your company was involved in combing the terrain. Now, on direct examination, you indicated that you were put under the Bratunac Brigade during the searching of the terrain on the 17th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that you had some sort of order allowing that to occur.

utterances.speaker: DUSKO JEVIC
utterances.text: All orders throughout that period of time, sir, were oral orders. They were orally transmitted. Now, whether the officers at the Bratunac Brigade had any written orders, I can't say. What I can say is on the 16th, I reported to Mr. Nikolic in the evening. On the 17th, I attended the meeting. The task was agreed; the deployment of the forces was agreed. And the communications modalities were agreed, the start line was agreed. And as far as that's concerned, I have nothing further to add.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, we're almost out of time, Your Honour, I believe. However, perhaps, if could be so kind overnight while you're visiting The Hague here, you could look over the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor back on 18 October 2000. And perhaps overnight, you can look in it, and you can search it, and you can tell us where exactly in your statement you indicate that you were subordinate to the Bratunac Brigade, that you were asked to meet with Momir Nikolic on the 16th, and how the Bratunac Brigade was in charge of this operation. And we'll pick up from there tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not clear if that was a rhetorical question or a homework assignment --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A homework assignment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- Your Honour, he's come a long way. I don't know if he has the statement. But there's a lot of logistics involved in such a request that need to be taken care of if it's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have the statement. It's copied. I can give it to him. I can direct him. It's 70 pages, but he only needs to read about 20. I understand the gentleman may want to walk around the town and see a little bit of The Hague. But we're in the middle of a trial, and I can do it tomorrow page by page. It will take us a lot of time. I don't care. Either way, Your Honour. But I want the gentleman to see where -- to show me exactly where it is in the statement because I haven't been able to find it. Maybe it's there someplace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is rhetoric, this is game playing. It's not serious. If it's not there, it's not there. And that's the question. But if he truly wants this witness to see his statement, I have no objection to that. But it's hard for me to separate the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could I understand that there's no argument, no debate, no different views on that previous statement that the matter of resubordination is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. But also, I am going to be going page-by-page where there are references to where they are searching together. And also, with respect to who handles the prisoners that they come across, the number of the prisoners. And so, I will be going through that in great detail with the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think in response to your question, Your Honour, there is certain things in his previous statement that he does say that he believes the MUP is under the command of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's utterly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't want counsel to argue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My recollection is he says that, Your Honour. And that he said that he believed General Krstic was in charge, and I believe he spoke about the rules in his previous statement. So just to answer your question, there may be a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since the Prosecution is not against this kind of practice, and in the past we have done so during the break, I believe that after the sitting, the Registrar will provide a copy of the statement of this witness for him to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which might - might - save some time for tomorrow's proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm afraid you have to stay here for another day. And during your stay in The Hague, you have to remember that you are a witness in these proceedings, and you are under the oath. So do not talk to anybody or do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.
